title: Linux Basics 1
readme:
Linux Basics 1

You are the administrator of this workstation. A security review found problems. Fix them without breaking what the company needs.

Authorized administrators:
  • you (the account you are logged in with)

Authorized users:
  • alice
  • bob

Company policy:
  • Only authorized users may have accounts on this computer.
  • Only authorized administrators may have administrator (sudo) rights.
  • The host firewall must be turned on.
  • User passwords must expire after at most 90 days.
  • Sensitive system files must not be readable by everyone.

Do not delete authorized users. There are 5 problems, 20 points each. Your score updates in PT Comp about every 20 seconds.
setup:
set -e
# Plants the 5 problems. Every problem is forced into place, so a VM someone already hardened
# still starts the practice with all 5.
pw() { printf '%s' "$(tr -dc 'A-Za-z0-9' </dev/urandom | head -c 14)Aa1!"; }
for u in alice bob hacker; do
    id "$u" >/dev/null 2>&1 || useradd -m -s /bin/bash "$u"
    echo "$u:$(pw)" | chpasswd
done
# 1) hacker exists (unauthorized). 2) bob is an administrator, but only you should be.
usermod -aG sudo bob
# 3) the firewall is off
command -v ufw >/dev/null || { echo "ufw is not installed on this VM" >&2; exit 1; }
ufw --force disable >/dev/null
# 4) passwords never expire
if grep -qE '^[[:space:]]*PASS_MAX_DAYS' /etc/login.defs; then
    sed -i -E 's/^[[:space:]]*PASS_MAX_DAYS.*/PASS_MAX_DAYS\t99999/' /etc/login.defs
else
    printf 'PASS_MAX_DAYS\t99999\n' >> /etc/login.defs
fi
# 5) everyone can read the password hashes
chmod 644 /etc/shadow

checks.message: bob is no longer an administrator
Passwords expire after at most 90 days
Only root (and the shadow group) can read /etc/shadow
